title: Great Adamz and Maddox Jones Explore Love and Heartbreak on New Collaboration “Letting Go”
description: Produced by Manuel Riva, the R&B-pop collaboration explores the complicated realities of love, heartbreak and knowing when to let go. Love is rarely as straightforward as people want it to be.
coverAlt: Great Adamz and Maddox Jones Explore Love and Heartbreak on New Collaboration “Letting Go”

body.text: Produced by Manuel Riva, the R&B-pop collaboration explores the complicated realities of love, heartbreak and knowing when to let go.

Love is rarely as straightforward as people want it to be. Between the moments that bring two people together and the experiences that gradually pull them apart, relationships can leave behind questions, memories and emotions that are difficult to put into words. It is this emotional territory that Great Adamz and Maddox Jones explore on their new collaboration, Letting Go, produced by internationally recognised Romanian DJ and producer Manuel Riva.

Blending R&B and contemporary pop, [Letting Go](https://lnk.to/letting-go) explores the complexities of relationships, from the highs of falling in love to the heartbreak, uncertainty and emotional weight that can come with trying to hold on. The collaboration brings together Great Adamz’s distinctive vocal delivery and Maddox Jones’s emotionally driven pop sensibility, creating a meeting of sounds that complements the song’s central theme.

For Great Adamz, the release arrives during a significant period in his musical journey. The artist continues to build an international profile through a combination of chart success, cross-genre collaborations and growing industry recognition. His single Shake, produced in collaboration with Manuel Riva, has received Grammy consideration, marking his second consecutive year receiving consideration from the Recording Academy.

The achievement follows a run of successful releases that has seen Great Adamz establish a presence across Afrobeats, Afrofusion, pop and dance music. His catalogue includes records such as Funke, Jeje and Umada, with Funke now experiencing renewed chart momentum in the UK, introducing the track to audiences once again and adding to the growing conversation around his music.

His partnership with Manuel Riva has also demonstrated his willingness to explore new sonic territory. Riva, known for his internationally successful electronic and dance productions, brings a distinctive production approach to their collaborations, creating space for Great Adamz’s vocals to move across different musical landscapes.

Maddox Jones brings another dimension to Letting Go. The British singer-songwriter has built his career around honest songwriting, memorable melodies and emotionally resonant pop, with a sound shaped by indie, pop and soul influences. His ability to translate personal experiences into relatable songs makes him a natural creative counterpart for a record centred on the difficult realities of love and relationships.

Together, Great Adamz and Maddox Jones approach Letting Go as a collaboration between two artists rather than a traditional featured-artist arrangement, allowing their individual styles to contribute to a shared musical identity. With Manuel Riva behind the production, the record brings together distinct creative perspectives around a theme that remains universally relatable.

As Great Adamz continues to expand his catalogue and build on his recent achievements, Letting Go represents another step in his evolving sound — one that places emotion, vocal expression and cross-genre collaboration at the forefront.

title: The UK Isn’t Telling You To Stockpile Because Russia Is Coming - Here's The Real Story
description: A viral post making the rounds online has left many people with the impression that the UK government has suddenly told households to start stocking up on food and water because Britain is preparing for war with Russia.
coverAlt: The UK Isn’t Telling You To Stockpile Because Russia Is Coming - Here's The Real Story

body.text: A viral post making the rounds online has left many people with the impression that the UK government has suddenly told households to start stocking up on food and water because Britain is preparing for war with Russia.
That is not the full story.

The image circulating online — which we’ve also included with this report — frames the announcement as the UK urging households to stock food and water for “potential war with Russia, cyber attacks and extreme weather.”
There is some truth behind the claim, but the wording makes several different parts of Britain’s national resilience planning sound like one single warning about an imminent war.
Here’s what is actually happening.
So, Why Is The UK Asking People To Keep Food And Water At Home?
The UK government has been developing a national resilience public-awareness campaign designed to get households better prepared for emergencies and disruption.
And this campaign was announced months before the latest viral posts.

In July, the government said the campaign would encourage people to take “small but important steps” to prepare for emergencies — including severe weather and cyber attacks that could disrupt access to power, water, phone networks or local shops.
The government is also developing materials for a three-year household resilience campaign, which is expected to launch later this year.
So no, this isn't simply a sudden instruction telling Britons: “Russia is coming, go and buy tins.”
But Is Russia Part Of The Reason?
Yes — but this is where the story gets complicated.
Britain is genuinely strengthening its preparations for serious national-security scenarios.

The government is updating its contingency plans for a major conflict or threat to the UK, traditionally known as the War Book. It is also planning a major home-defence exercise in 2027 to test how government and public services would respond to a serious national crisis.
Russia's actions and the wider security situation in Europe are part of the reason these preparations have received renewed attention.
But preparing for a possible security scenario is not the same thing as announcing that war with Russia is about to happen.
That distinction matters.
The UK's National Risk Register is designed to assess serious risks that could affect the country. It is explicitly a planning tool, not a prediction.
And those risks go far beyond military conflict.
They include things such as cyber attacks, infrastructure disruption, extreme weather, disease outbreaks and other events capable of disrupting normal life.
Then There Is The Weather
This is another major part of the conversation that has been lost in the viral “Russia is coming” framing.
The UK is currently paying close attention to El Niño, a climate pattern developing in the Pacific that scientists expect to become significant towards the end of 2026.
The UK Government Office for Science published a rapid assessment on 17 September examining its possible impact on Britain.

It says the effects on UK weather are less certain, but there could be a slightly increased chance of stronger westerly winds, low-pressure systems, storminess, heavy rainfall and flooding between October and December 2026. Early 2027 could also bring a slightly increased risk of easterly or northerly winds and cold snaps.
There could also be knock-on effects through global food and energy markets.
The important word here is could.
Scientists are not saying Britain is definitely about to experience some unprecedented weather disaster. The government's own assessment stresses that the UK effects remain uncertain.
And Yes, Germany Is Preparing Too
You may also have seen reports about Germany preparing its hospitals for a potential military conflict.
That part is real — but some social media posts have made it sound much more dramatic than it is.
Germany has been conducting exercises and reviewing how its civilian and military healthcare systems would cope with large numbers of wounded people in a NATO conflict scenario.

A Bundeswehr exercise in March 2026 specifically tested patient transport and healthcare arrangements, with German military planners considering scenarios involving hundreds, potentially up to around 1,000, wounded or sick people requiring treatment each day.
That does not mean Germany has closed hospitals because war is coming.
It means Germany, like other European countries, is examining whether its healthcare infrastructure would be able to cope with a major emergency.
So What Are British Households Actually Being Asked To Do?
Nothing particularly dramatic.
The broader preparedness guidance is essentially about having enough basic supplies to cope if normal services are temporarily disrupted.
Think:
Drinking water
Non-perishable food
Torches
Batteries
A power bank
Radio
First-aid supplies
Essential medication
Supplies for babies and pets where necessary

The government's 2026 public survey also shows why officials are pushing the issue: only 37% of surveyed households said they had enough bottled water to last three days, while 85% reported having at least three days' worth of non-perishable food.

In other words, the basic idea is not particularly new or extraordinary: if something disrupts normal life for a few days, don't be completely dependent on the supermarket being open, the electricity working or the water supply being uninterrupted.
So, Is This About Russia?
Russia is part of the wider security picture. It is not the whole explanation.
Britain is preparing for a range of scenarios: extreme weather, cyber attacks, infrastructure failures, supply disruptions and national-security threats, including the possibility of conflict.
The mistake is taking all of that and reducing it to:
“The UK is telling everyone to stockpile because Russia is coming.”
That is a much stronger claim than the evidence supports.
The image circulating online isn't completely detached from reality — but it compresses a much broader national-resilience programme into a single frightening headline.
And that distinction is important.
Britain is preparing.
Germany is preparing.
Governments across Europe are reviewing their emergency systems.
El Niño is developing.
Security risks are real.
But none of those facts, by themselves, mean that war with Russia is imminent.

The sensible takeaway is much simpler: governments are asking people to be better prepared for disruption — while they simultaneously strengthen their own plans for everything from severe weather and cyber attacks to serious security crises.
That's the real story.

title: Great Adamz Shines as Best Singer of the Year at MK Afro Diaspora Awards 2026
description: Milton Keynes, UK — September 2026UK-based Afropop/Afrofusion artist Great Adamz has added another major accolade to his growing list of achievements after being crowned Best Singer of the Year at the 2026 MK Afro Diaspora Awards.
coverAlt: Great Adamz Shines as Best Singer of the Year at MK Afro Diaspora Awards 2026

body.text: Milton Keynes, UK — September 2026
UK-based Afropop/Afrofusion artist Great Adamz has added another major accolade to his growing list of achievements after being crowned Best Singer of the Year at the 2026 MK Afro Diaspora Awards.

The recognition was presented at the fourth edition of the MK Afro Diaspora Awards, held on 5 September 2026 at Medbourne Pavilion in Milton Keynes. The award celebrates Great Adamz’s continued contribution to music and his growing impact within the African diaspora community in the UK.

For the artist, the recognition comes at a significant point in his career. Following a run of chart appearances, award wins and growing international attention, being named Best Singer of the Year further reinforces his position as one of the UK-based African artists steadily building a presence both within and beyond the music scene.
About the MK Afro Diaspora Awards

The MK Afro Diaspora Awards is an annual recognition platform celebrating the achievements, contributions and impact of Black African and Caribbean individuals, businesses and organisations within the Milton Keynes community.

The 2026 edition was organised by Might and Grace Productions CIC, a Milton Keynes-based organisation involved in creative, cultural, entertainment and community-focused initiatives. The organisation is led by Anthonia Ngozi Beddall, whose work spans community engagement, event development, creative programming and opportunities for artists and creative practitioners.

Now in its fourth edition, the awards recognise excellence across entertainment, community support, fashion, hair and beauty, business and innovation, catering and hospitality, youth, sports, and health and wellbeing. The platform continues to shine a light on individuals whose work, talent and contributions are helping strengthen the African and Caribbean community in Milton Keynes.
Another Milestone in a Growing Career:
Great Adamz’s latest recognition comes on the back of an increasingly impressive run.

His recent single “Omahe” has been gaining strong traction across social media, particularly on TikTok, where audiences have embraced the song’s uplifting sound and feel-good energy. The release also climbed to No. 6 on the iTunes African: Nigeria chart within days of its release and reached No. 11 on the iTunes Music: Nigeria chart.

His previous single “Shake,” a collaboration with international dance producer Manuel Riva, delivered another significant milestone, reaching No. 1 on the Music Week Black Music Chart — Great Adamz’s first appearance on the chart — while also surpassing **1 million plays on Audiomack.

Beyond his music, Great Adamz has continued to receive recognition for his contribution to the wider African and diaspora community, building a reputation that extends beyond recordings and performances.

With the momentum continuing to build, the artist is expected to take his music to bigger stages across the UK and diaspora, with more performances, tours and international opportunities ahead. He is also preparing for upcoming projects and live appearances, including his Hearts & Harmony Valentine's event.
The Best Singer of the Year award marks another significant chapter in Great Adamz’s journey — and with “Omahe” continuing to gain momentum, there is clearly more to come.
Congratulations to Great Adamz on this well-deserved recognition.

title: Great Adamz’s “Omahe” Climbs to No. 6 on iTunes African: Nigeria Chart, Peaks at No. 5

body.text: Northampton-based Afropop artist Great Adamz continues to make waves internationally as his latest single, “Omahe,” climbs to No. 6 on the iTunes African: Nigeria chart, following a peak at No. 5 just days after its release.

The latest milestone adds to an impressive run for the Northampton artist, who has continued to build a strong presence across the UK and international Afropop scene. Omahe is also making an impact on the wider Nigerian iTunes chart, currently sitting at No. 11 on the Music: Nigeria chart, after reaching a peak of No. 8.

Released as a softer and more reflective offering, Omahe explores themes of love, joy, spirituality and human connection. The record carries a warm, peaceful energy, while its accompanying visual features African children dancing, playing and enjoying moments of genuine happiness — reinforcing the song's message of innocence, community and togetherness.
The chart movement is another notable milestone for Great Adamz, who has steadily established himself as one of Northampton's prominent Afropop exports while developing an audience beyond the UK.

His recent collaboration Shake with Romanian producer Manuel Riva reached No. 1 on the Music Week Black Music Top 20 Club Chart and surpassed one million Audiomack plays, adding to a growing list of career achievements.
From Northampton to audiences across Africa and beyond, Omahe represents another chapter in Great Adamz's evolving sound — one rooted in love, culture, positivity and connection.
And with the record continuing to climb the Nigerian charts, the Northampton artist is proving once again that his reach extends far beyond his hometown.

title: Inside Erigga & Eeskay’s Exclusive North & South EP UK Listening Party, Hosted by Music Publicist Chinenye Mbakwe
description: BIRMINGHAM, UK — Nigerian rap heavyweight Erigga and rising talent Eeskay gave fans an unforgettable first experience of their collaborative EP, North & South, at an exclusive UK listening party held in Birmingham, bringing together music…
coverAlt: Inside Erigga & Eeskay’s Exclusive North & South EP UK Listening Party, Hosted by Music Publicist Chinenye Mbakwe

body.text: BIRMINGHAM, UK — Nigerian rap heavyweight Erigga and rising talent Eeskay gave fans an unforgettable first experience of their collaborative EP, North & South, at an exclusive UK listening party held in Birmingham, bringing together music lovers, creatives, media personalities and members of the African entertainment community for an intimate evening celebrating one of the year’s most anticipated hip-hop projects.

The listening experience offered attendees an opportunity to hear the project before many audiences around the world, while also giving fans a deeper understanding of the stories, themes and creative direction behind the collaboration. Throughout the evening, conversations around the EP highlighted Erigga’s signature storytelling, Eeskay’s distinctive style and the chemistry that makes North & South a standout collaborative body of work.

Hosted by Music Publicist Chinenye Mbakwe of 99PLUZ, the event went beyond simply playing music. Guests were taken through an immersive listening experience that encouraged discussion, audience participation and meaningful engagement with the project.

As host for the evening, Mbakwe guided the programme, welcomed guests and facilitated conversations around the EP, engaging attendees while exploring the creative direction behind the project and its place within today’s Nigerian hip-hop landscape. Her role also reflected the growing importance of music publicists and public speakers in creating memorable experiences that connect artists directly with audiences beyond traditional performances.

Representing 99PLUZ, Mbakwe helped create an atmosphere where fans could not only listen to the music but also connect with the stories behind it, reinforcing the role of listening parties as important moments for artist development, fan engagement and cultural exchange.

The event further demonstrated the continued growth of African music within the United Kingdom, particularly in cities such as Birmingham, where audiences continue to embrace Nigerian music through live experiences, community events and artist showcases.

For Erigga and Eeskay, the evening marked another important milestone in the rollout of North & South, allowing supporters to experience the project collectively before continuing its journey across streaming platforms worldwide. The atmosphere throughout the night reflected the strong anticipation surrounding the release, with attendees responding enthusiastically to the project’s lyricism, production and authentic storytelling.

Speaking after the event, attendees praised the intimate nature of the listening experience, describing it as an opportunity to engage with the music in a more personal setting while celebrating Nigerian hip-hop with fellow fans.

With North & South now available to listeners worldwide, Erigga and Eeskay continue to build momentum around the project, further cementing their place within the evolving landscape of African hip-hop.

title: Great Adamz Unveils “Omahe,” a Heartwarming Celebration of Love, Joy and Togetherness

coverAlt: Great Adamz Unveils “Omahe,” a Heartwarming Celebration of Love, Joy and Togetherness

body.text: Grammy-considered UK Afropop artist Great Adamz returns with “Omahe,” a heartfelt new single that celebrates love, hope, and the simple beauty of human connection.

Following the success of recent releases that showcased his versatility and global sound, Omahe reveals a more reflective side of the artist. Built around warm melodies, soothing instrumentation, and uplifting vocals, the record creates an atmosphere of peace while reminding listeners to embrace life’s most meaningful moments.

The accompanying visual mirrors that message. Set against scenes of children playing, dancing, and sharing moments of genuine happiness, the music video captures the innocence, joy, and togetherness that define the heart of the song. Rather than relying on spectacle, Omahe finds its strength in authentic human emotion, portraying a world where love, community, and gratitude take centre stage.

For Great Adamz, the record represents another step in his artistic evolution. While known for blending Afropop with contemporary global influences, Omahe leans into a softer, more spiritual energy—one that invites listeners to pause, reflect, and appreciate the people and moments that truly matter.

The release follows a remarkable period for the UK-based artist, whose recent achievements include multiple No. 1 records on the Music Week Black Music Top 20 Club Chart, over one million Audiomack plays for Shake, sold-out headline performances, and continued recognition for pushing UK Afropop onto the global stage.

With Omahe, Great Adamz delivers more than a song—it is a reminder that joy can be found in simplicity, that love remains universal, and that music continues to be one of the most powerful ways to bring people together.
